articles.title: A good friend brings her dogs when she stays with me. I kind of dread it. What can I do? | Leading questions
articles.summary: People often forget social rules when dogs are involved, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. But you’ll have to say something if you want things to change. A good friend of mine stays with me regularly when she comes into town.
body: Eleanor says: It sounds as though you’re in the jam we all get into when we try to smooth things over: you can have the social ease of pretending something is fine; or the outcome from confessing it isn’t, but not both simultaneously.

Obviously, your friend should have paid more mind to the possibility that you don’t see her dogs like she does. Using the bathroom in your house? The first rule of society is that other people’s preferences might differ from yours, and that matters for how you treat them and their stuff.

But bring a dog into the equation and some otherwise intelligent people seem to forget that. They’ll trail behind on a leash giving the choreography of an apology while their dog puts paws on tables, bounds excitedly up to frightened children or treats furniture and food the way they’re allowed to at home. I’m saying this as a lifelong Dog Person, for what it’s worth: there is not a muddy paw print in the world I mind if it means I am playing with a dog. But we must admit, some dog people give the rest of us a bad name by assuming everyone sees their dog the way they do.
points: People often forget social rules when dogs are involved, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith.
But you’ll have to say something if you want things to change.

articles.title: I spent years postponing my own joy. Here’s how I learned to say yes to the juicy bits of life | Sheree Joseph
articles.summary: Society tells us there is one way to live a life, and joy is a byproduct on the path there. But you don’t need a reason to enjoy the act of being alive. I have been dwelling on what it means to live well. Not because I have mastered it, but because I have become very comically bad at it.
body: But most of all I became fixated on my fertility and how it dwindled in my early 30s, leaving me to make choices most women don’t have to until later. I tried to save my eggs and couldn’t. My lack of a partner in a conservative Catholic Lebanese family became a cudgel.
Pleasure was something bypassed on the way to a goal of being chosen and accepted. In other words, joy was a byproduct.
Trying to live well in a society that doesn’t prioritise it is like filling a cup with the bottom cut off: the water just runs through, passing you by, leaving you as parched as sandpaper.

A holiday was an opportunity to recover from work. In Italy, the plastic cup in my hand was solid and filled with the bitter strength of a negroni sbagliato – or a “broken negroni” – a drink whose name comes from the fact it was first made by mistake.
points: Society tells us there is one way to live a life, and joy is a byproduct on the path there.
But you don’t need a reason to enjoy the act of being alive.

articles.title: The fashion industry wants women to wear bras again - but is underwire the answer?
articles.summary: From Charli xcx and Rihanna to Victoria’s Secret and Prada catwalks, the fashion industry is keen to move on from the comfy, wire-free bras popularized in lockdown. It’s a trend which might have been expected to be kept under the radar – or at least under a T-shirt.
body: This fashion month, underwear as outerwear was omnipresent on catwalks, with underwire bras in red and black satin at Prada and black and silver at Tom Ford. At the Matieres Fecales show, Rihanna wore a bra from her own Savage X Fenty range peeking out of her unbuttoned jacket.

Elsewhere, Anya Taylor Joy wore a Balmain fuchsia underwire bra, with a cardigan and a floral jacquard skirt while promoting her new series. Model Kaia Gerber recently wore a wool crepe Alaïa bra top on the red carpet, which featured an exposed underwire as part of the design.

At the VMAs, Tyla wore a blue snakeskin-print by Mowalola with a matching low-rise skirt. Mowalola Ogunlesi, the London-based designer behind the look, says her thinking was that “I’m finding power in femininity and treating lingerie as something complete in itself, rather than something that needs to be hidden or layered”. An underwire bra was the basis of the outfit because, she says, “it sculpts the body in a unique way”.
points: From Charli xcx and Rihanna to Victoria’s Secret and Prada catwalks, the fashion industry is keen to move on from the comfy, wire-free bras popularized in lockdown.

articles.title: For These Stylish Brooklyn Preschool Teachers, Fashion Is Part of the Pedagogy
articles.summary: “[Children] can grow up in a beautiful place and know that those things are important,” says Stephanie Woo, head of Ms. Lam Montessori School.
body: Stephanie Woo, the head of Ms. Lam Montessori School, joins our Zoom dressed in a tightly pleated salmon button-up shirt. Though she’s calling in from Taiwan just after midnight, Woo looks ready for a full day at one of her five campuses across Brooklyn: all of the staffers at Ms. Lam wear colorful micropleated dresses and smocks that bear a striking resemblance to Pleats Please, Issey Miyake ’s beloved line of lightweight separates in every color under the sun.

Yesterday, a post on the Williamsburg neighborhood subreddit went viral on Reddit—and later on X—about the ultra-stylish teachers at Ms. Lam. “[D]oes anyone know what the deal is Ms Lam Montessori…and why all their employees wear Issey Miyake (a very expensive and distinct Japanese designer) every day?” a user posted. “It’s true,” another person wrote on X. “These Brooklyn teachers are seriously dripped out in Issey Miyake.”

body: So, looking at the date on my Garmin Forerunner 970, I can see that Amazon's October Prime Day sale is officially over. But if you missed your chance to upgrade your running watch, you're in luck: Two of the most popular Garmin Forerunners are still on sale, even after Prime Day has technically ended.

The Garmin Forerunner 55 is $161.99, down from $199.99. This is the most basic Garmin running watch you can buy new. Don't be deterred by the word "basic." As my colleague Beth Skwarecki reports, it was good enough for Sabastian Sawe to wear to break the sub-2-hour marathon barrier earlier this year.
The Garmin Forerunner 165 is $199.99, down from $249.99. This is my favorite entry-level running watch. The music version is also on sale; as always, it runs $50 more than the standard.

While it's not a dramatic, the Garmin Forerunner 265 is 5% off, bringing the original price of $449.99 down to $429. Although it isn't the latest and greatest anymore, this is still a fan favorite among Garmin users. It's a step above entry-level options, with dual-band GPS, power meter compatibility, and advanced analytics (like training status).

articles.title: Vogue Editors Pick Their Favorite Spring 2027 Shows
articles.summary: Vogue editors and contributors attended 440 spring 2027 shows between New York and Paris. These are our standout collections of the season.
body: From Ralph Lauren in New York to Louis Vuitton in Paris, Vogue Runway’s editors and contributors logged a lot of miles over the last month, attending and reviewing—count ’em—440 spring 2027 shows and presentations. That’s a lot of fashion! What sticks out? What will we remember a year from now, or 10?

A good measure is the zinging sensation of an adrenaline surge that you get when a show really connects. “Full body tingles,” is the way Sarah Mower put it to me. It’s an individual feeling and, often, a collective one. At the very best shows, you can register the audience’s vibes in the body language running along a bench, everyone eagle-eyed, camera phone at the ready, angling for the best possible view. This season, these were our standouts.

Where individual pairs of dumbbells from five to 80 pounds in five-pound increments would cost well over $1,500 (and take up your entire home gym), adjustable dumbbells condense an entire weight rack into a compact, versatile system. Here are the best deals on adjustable dumbbells that you can still snag, at least for the next few hours.

My favorite deal right now is this set of Bowflex Results Series 552 dumbbells, $328.98 for a pair, normally $399.99. If you couldn’t guess from the name, they can adjust from five to 52 pounds. The curved design is stylish, but more importantly, it's a seriously space-saving—which is the whole point of going adjustable over a traditional rack of individual weights.
NordicTrack Select-a-Weight Adjustable Dumbbells are $319, normally $399. Each dumbbell in this set can adjust up to 55 pounds, with 2.5, five, and 10-pound increments available.

articles.title: The Entire Samsung Galaxy S26 Lineup Is Still on Sale After October Prime Day
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Deal pricing and availability subject to change after time of publication. Samsung makes a lot of devices, but if you want the best of its "traditional" smartphones, your only option is the Galaxy S series, including the current Galaxy S26 series.
body: The cheapest of the bunch is the Galaxy S26 FE. This is the "budget" model of the Galaxy S26 line, but still a great phone in its own right. It comes with a 6.7-inch AMOLED display with three rear cameras: a 50MP wide, 12MP ultrawide, and an 8MP telephoto. (You also get a 12MP selfie camera.) It has a 4900mAh battery, runs the Exynos 2500 chip, and 8GB of RAM with either 128GB or 256GB of storage.

But for the best Samsung has to offer, choose the Galaxy S26 Ultra. This option comes with Samsung's biggest and best display, a 6.9-inch AMOLED with the same solution as the Galaxy S26+. It has Samsung's best cameras, too: a 200MP wide lens, a 10MP telephoto lens, a 50MP periscope lens, and a 50MP ultrawide. It has a 5000mAh battery and either 12GB or 16GB of RAM—if you opt for the 1TB model.
